prerequisites: Basic knowledge of Physics, Mathematics, Chemistry, and Thermodynamics

learning_outcomes.text: Determine which aspects of the natural environment can be susceptible to industrial impacts.
Know what mechanisms exist to integrate industrial activities into the environment.
Learn strategies and tools for minimizing and correcting environmental impacts caused by industry.
Generate responsible attitudes towards the environment from professional activity in their specialty.
Have the ability to apply knowledge for the reduction, reuse, recycling or valorization of waste generated by society and its industrial activities.

Understand that currently waste management is an activity with a high industrial component, essential for the sustainable development of societies, requiring the transformation of waste into resources.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to environmental engineering. Brief historical review of pollution problems. Definitions. Classifications. Basic principles of waste management.
Sound and noise. Physical parameters. Acoustic indices. Regulations. Effects of noise on living beings. Measurement equipment.
Natural and anthropogenic electromagnetic field. Physical parameters. EMF-generating technologies. Effects. Regulations.
Atmospheric composition. Atmospheric pollutants. Direct and indirect effects. Emission and immission. Treatment technologies. Pollutant dispersion. Regulations.

Water on Earth. Residence time. Water quality. Anthropogenic and natural pollution. Water characterization. Regulations. Purification. Soil as a resource. Soil degradation. Endogenous and exogenous contamination. Soil-polluting industries.
Principles of waste management. Definitions, classification and properties. Legislation, regulation and planning. Main waste flows.
Separation. Collection systems. Treatment systems. Prevention.
Regulations. Environmental audits and Environmental Management Systems (EMS). EMAS registry.
Basic operations for waste processing and separation. Size reduction techniques. Size and density separation. Magnetic and electric field separation. Densification and compaction.
Ferrous and non-ferrous metals. Polymers. Glass and ceramics. Paper and cardboard.
assessment_rules: Evaluation follows either a Continuous Evaluation (EvC) or Single Evaluation (EvU) path. For EvC, assessment comprises short-answer tests (50%), laboratory/field practices (20%), and a final project (30%). A minimum grade of 5/10 is required in the final short-answer test, with both modules needing independent approval; otherwise, the final grade is 50% of the test grade. For EvU, assessment includes an exam (60%), a practice (20%), and an individual project (20%). A minimum grade of 5/10 is required in the EvU exam to pass the course; otherwise, the final grade is the exam grade. Grades from successfully completed practices in EvC or previous years can be conserved.
